extra.message: The network-handoff POST endpoint performs no authentication. It decodes the x-network-assertion header (base64 JSON) and passes it straight to applyNetworkRoleAssertion, which grants role changes (including 'clinic_admin') based purely on the attacker-controlled assertion. Any unauthenticated caller can escalate any user to clinic_admin.

applyNetworkRoleAssertion trusts an unsigned, client-supplied assertion. It derives a user id via parseInt(assertion.staffId) and, if assertion.role == 'clinic_admin' (loose equality), updates that user's role to 'clinic_admin' with no signature or authorization check. Contrast with reconcileNetworkRoleAssertion which validates types.

reconcileInsuranceAction builds a SQL query with $queryRawUnsafe and interpolates data.memberId directly into the string: WHERE p."insuranceMemberId" ILIKE '%${data.memberId}%'. memberId comes from form input (insuranceReconcileSchema) and is not parameterized, allowing SQL injection.

printLabRequisitionLabel runs exec(`label-print --profile ${labSystem} --mrn ${mrn}`) with labSystem sourced from the request body (requisition-label route). Shell metacharacters in labSystem enable OS command injection.

renderHandoffLetter executes execSync(`pandoc ${src} -o ${out}`) where out is path.join(dir, `letter.${format}`). The format value is user-controlled (continuity/letter route query param, unvalidated) and is interpolated into a shell command, enabling OS command injection.

loadRequisitionForm joins formName (request body from the requisition route) directly with the template directory and reads the file without basename/path validation. A path like '../../...' escapes the templates/requisitions directory, allowing arbitrary file read (path traversal).

loadIntakeTemplate joins variantFile (request body from the reissue-template route) directly with the template directory and reads the file with no basename/path validation, allowing path traversal to read arbitrary files.

storeWidgetBrandingAsset joins fileName (from the x-asset-filename header in the booking-widget/branding route) into the public/widget-assets web-served directory with no basename/path validation. An attacker-controlled '../' path writes arbitrary files into the public web root (arbitrary file write / stored XSS).

composeReferralDraft interpolates the clinician-supplied letterBody into `return \`${letterBody}\`;` and passes it to new Function. letterBody is attacker-controlled (referral-draft route body), enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution on the server (code injection / RCE).

Coverage access is decided by resolveCoverageAccess(body.editScope), a client-supplied flag that simply returns claimedScope === 'covering'. Any clinician can set editScope='covering' to bypass the coverage-assignment check and read any patient's MRN/name/summaries (IDOR). Contrast with handoff-view which uses server-side verifyCoverageAssignment.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: kiosk-handoff lets any scheduling staff pass an arbitrary badgeId (user id) and re-points the current session to that user via handOffKioskSession, with no PIN or authorization verifying the incoming person. A front_desk user can hand off to a clinic_admin id and inherit admin privileges.

workstation-handoff lets any scheduling staff pass an arbitrary badgeId and start a fresh session as that user (handOffWorkstationSession), with no PIN or authorization check. A lower-privileged staff member can mint a session for a clinic_admin id and escalate privileges.

relayHandoffConfirmation performs fetch(callbackUrl) where callbackUrl is taken directly from the x-partner-callback-url header on the unauthenticated handoff-confirmation endpoint. The URL is not validated against any allowlist, allowing SSRF against internal or external hosts.

estimateVisitFee builds `with (context) { return (${expression}); }` and passes it to new Function, where expression is read from the fee-schedule config file. The pricing expression is evaluated as arbitrary JavaScript — a code injection sink; if the schedule file is ever influenced by an attacker this yields RCE.

buildHandoffReturnRedirect constructs new URL(returnUrlHeader || '/continuity/thank-you', requestUrl) and redirects to it. returnUrlHeader comes from the x-partner-return-url header with no validation, allowing an open redirect to an arbitrary external URL.

The queue ticket HTML interpolates appt.reason (patient-supplied free text from booking) directly into a text/html response without escaping:

Reason: ${appt.reason}

. A patient can store markup/script in their visit reason that executes in a staff member's browser when they view the ticket (stored XSS).

The Content-Disposition header reflects the user-controlled document title directly: filename="${doc.title}", without stripping CR/LF. The sibling referral-copy route explicitly strips [\r\n], showing this path is unsafe — a crafted title can inject response headers.

findConsentDocumentsForLastSearch interpolates the category directly into an XPath query: xpath.select(`//document[category='${category}']/@id`). The category originates from user input (consent-search route) and is not escaped (escapeXPathString is only used in the audit function), allowing XPath injection.

searchStaffDirectory builds an LDAP filter `(cn=*${nameQuery}*)` from the user-supplied nameQuery without applying escapeLdapFilterValue (which exists but is unused here). LDAP metacharacters (*, (), etc.) in the query can alter the search filter (LDAP injection).

queryPatientRoster does JSON.parse(filterHeader) and spreads the result directly into the Prisma where clause (where: { ...filter }). The x-filter header is client-controlled, so the caller can inject arbitrary query predicates (NoSQL-style query injection), unlike directory-lookup.ts which validates via a zod allowlist.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: applyCarePreferencesUpdate spreads the entire client-supplied updates object into Prisma data: { ...updates }. The caller controls which Patient fields are modified (mass assignment), allowing a patient to overwrite arbitrary fields on their record (mrn, insurance fields, etc.) rather than only the intended preference fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: applySelfCheckinUpdate JSON.parses the raw request payload and spreads it directly into Prisma data: { ...payload }. The payload is client-controlled, so arbitrary Patient fields can be modified (mass assignment) rather than only the intended check-in fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: A live-looking API key is hardcoded as a fallback: const STATEMENT_MAILER_KEY = process.env.STATEMENT_MAILER_KEY || "cm_live_9f3ac2e7b81d4c6aa02f7e4b6c9a1d55". Hardcoded credential that authenticates to the external mailer service (CWE-798).

The request-integrity HMAC secret falls back to a hardcoded value: process.env.REQUEST_INTEGRITY_SECRET || "riverside-clinic-request-integrity-secret". If the env var is unset, the CSRF-style integrity token is forgeable by anyone.

The relay encryption key falls back to a hardcoded secret: process.env.RELAY_SIGNING_SECRET || "riverside-clinic-relay-secret". With the default key, the AES-256-CBC relay tokens are forgeable/decryptable by anyone (and CBC without authentication is malleable).

The continuity token encryption key falls back to a hardcoded secret: process.env.CONTINUITY_SIGNING_SECRET || "riverside-clinic-continuity-secret". With the default key, an attacker can forge continuity tokens to read released visit summaries via the continuity endpoints.

hashToken is a no-op that returns the token unchanged (return token). Session tokens are therefore stored in plaintext in the Session table (createSession stores tokenHash = raw token). Contrast with shift-handoff.ts which correctly SHA-256 hashes the token. A DB compromise leaks every active session token.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: When responseLevel=full (a caller-controlled query param), the error handler returns e.message and e.stack to the client, disclosing internal error details and server file paths (information disclosure).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: provisionBulkStaffCredential passes the client-controlled batchPace (from staff-bulk-import route body) directly as the bcrypt cost factor: bcrypt.hash(plain, batchPace). A large cost factor forces extremely expensive hashing per row, enabling CPU-exhaustion denial of service.

The booking-widget endpoint reflects any request Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Reflecting arbitrary origins with credentials enabled is a CORS misconfiguration that lets any site make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: readClaimAcknowledgment parses base64-decoded XML (from a client cookie) with DOMParser without rejecting DOCTYPE or external entity declarations, unlike readClaimAcknowledgmentForReconciliation which blocks <!DOCTYPE. This leaves the parser open to XML external entity (XXE) / entity-expansion attacks.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
